bill_summary: This bill extends the $14 million annual funding for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Program through fiscal year 2028. It also transfers the oversight and staffing of the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force from the Office of the Attorney General to the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) and allows DHCD to provide compensation or stipends to low-income tenant members of the task force.
responsible_party: Maryland Legal Services Corporation and the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Low-income tenants facing eviction, legal services organizations, the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, and landlords.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund revenues decrease by $14,000,000 in FY 2028 as funds are diverted from the Unclaimed Property Fund to the Access to Counsel in Evictions (ACE) Special Fund. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the ACE Special Fund increase by $14,000,000 in FY 2028 to continue the mandated appropriation for legal representation. The Department of Housing and Community Development can handle the task force's administrative changes and stipends with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Comptroller (as Administrator of the special fund for abandoned property) to distribute $14 million annually from the Unclaimed Property Fund to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund through fiscal 2028. Additionally, the Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Fund.

The bill transfers the appointment authority and staffing responsibilities for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force from the Office of the Attorney General to the Department of Housing and Community Development. The Secretary is also authorized to provide compensation to certain task force members.
The bill explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer shall hold the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund separately and invest the money of the Fund in the same manner as other State money.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership, staffing, and duties of the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force, which is a specialized study group within this government category.
The bill mandates that the Governor include a $14 million appropriation from the Fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation in the annual budget bill through fiscal 2028.

The bill transfers task force oversight away from the OAG to DHCD. However, the OAG's Division of Consumer Protection remains a revenue source for the Fund via settlements related to residential rental property investigations.
As the agency responsible for formulating the state budget, DBM must facilitate the Governor's mandated $14 million appropriation for the Access to Counsel in Evictions program.

The bill concerns legal representation in eviction proceedings which occur within the court system, and the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force is required to include representatives from the Judiciary.
The OLA is responsible for auditing state agencies and special funds; it would be responsible for auditing the fiscal compliance of the $14 million annual distribution and the ACE Special Fund.

bill_summary: This bill replaces remaining references to 'mental hygiene' with 'mental health' throughout the Health - General Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland. The Maryland Department of Health is required to update its regulations and public-facing electronic materials to reflect these changes by July 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland Department of Health, mental health service providers, and individuals receiving mental health services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's impact is minimal and can be managed with the Maryland Department of Health's existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact or impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency governing public health and the Behavioral Health Administration, the Department of Health is explicitly required by Section 2 of the bill to conduct a thorough review of its regulations and update all public-facing electronic materials to replace the term 'mental hygiene' with 'mental health'.
The bill explicitly amends § 24-1105(b) to direct the Comptroller to transfer investment earnings and proceeds into the renamed 'Mental Health Community-Based Services Fund.'

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal advisor to the Department of Health and will be responsible for providing legal counsel during the mandatory regulatory review and amendment process.

The State Treasurer's Office serves as the custodian of the state's financial assets and will be responsible for updating the nomenclature of the 'Mental Health Community-Based Services Fund' within the state's banking and investment records.

The bill amends § 10-208, which governs the sale or lease of Behavioral Health Administration facilities; the Board of Public Works is the administrative authority that reviews and approves such state property transactions and manages the resulting funds.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the Department of Health and signs the legislation to modernize state terminology regarding mental health services.

bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland's parole system by requiring the Maryland Parole Commission to consider an incarcerated individual's age during parole suitability determinations and establishing a specific geriatric parole process for individuals aged 65 and older who have served at least 20 years. It also updates the medical parole process by requiring physician-led health determinations, authorizing in-person meetings for infirm or hospitalized individuals, and repealing the Governor's authority to block medical parole decisions for individuals serving life sentences. Any savings from reduced incarceration must be reinvested into risk assessments, parole hearings, and reentry services.
responsible_party: Maryland Parole Commission and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals (specifically elderly or medically incapacitated individuals), the Maryland Parole Commission, the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and crime victims.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by an estimated $474,500 in FY 2026 to hire psychologists and administrative staff for required risk assessments, with costs rising to approximately $654,500 by FY 2030. These expenditures may be partially offset by indeterminate savings in incarceration costs (estimated at $5,339 per month per person), which the bill mandates be reinvested into assessments and reentry programs. There is no material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary implementing agency, as it oversees the Maryland Parole Commission and the correctional facilities where the individuals subject to this bill are currently housed. The bill directly impacts their operations regarding inmate processing, risk assessments, and parole hearing prioritization.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Office of the Public Defender is responsible for providing legal representation to indigent residents. This bill creates new pathways for parole for their clients (geriatric and medical populations), and their attorneys will be primarily responsible for filing requests and representing individuals in these expanded hearings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of GOCPP is a key figure in the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board (JROB). GOCPP also manages the Performance Incentive Grant Fund, which may be used to fund the Parole Commission's new responsibilities under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency designation includes the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board (JROB), which is specifically tasked by the bill to receive outcome reports from the Parole Commission and recommend the distribution of savings for the purpose of hiring psychologists and conducting risk assessments.

The bill repeals the Governor's existing authority to disapprove decisions by the Parole Commission to grant medical parole to incarcerated individuals serving life sentences, representing a significant change in the office's oversight powers.

The bill alters the criteria for medical parole based on determinations by licensed physicians regarding terminal illness and chronic debility, and it involves transitioning parolees into community-based medical management and hospice care.

The bill focuses on a geriatric population (65+) and the transition of individuals from incarceration to community-based care, which aligns with the department's mission to advocate for older adults and prepare infrastructure for the aging population.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to state agencies, including the Parole Commission and DPSCS. They will likely be involved in providing legal guidance on the new regulatory framework and the transition of medical parole authority.

The fiscal note indicates a significant increase in general fund expenditures ($474,500 in FY 2026) to implement the bill's requirements for risk assessments and psychologists, necessitating DBM's oversight of the budget and personnel changes.

The bill requires detailed annual reports on parole outcomes, reasons for denial/release, and recidivism rates. GOPI tracks these types of data-driven performance metrics across state agencies to identify opportunities for improvement and strategic planning.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration to revoke the driver's license of any individual convicted of, or granted probation before judgment for, driving while impaired by alcohol or drugs that contributes to an accident resulting in death or life-threatening injury. It also requires revocation for failing to remain at the scene of an accident resulting in death or serious bodily injury. The bill increases the wait time to apply for license reinstatement to five years, though the administration may allow for reinstatement after two years in cases of undue hardship or extenuating circumstances.
responsible_party: Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Drivers convicted of impaired driving resulting in death or life-threatening injury, drivers failing to remain at the scene of accidents involving death or serious injury, and the Maryland Department of Transportation.

MDOT is the parent agency of the MVA and requested this departmental legislation to enhance road safety and strengthen penalties for offenses resulting in death or life-threatening injury.
The OAH provides the Administrative Law Judges and impartial forum for the administrative appeals of driver’s license revocations mentioned in the bill.
The Maryland Judiciary is responsible for the convictions and probation before judgment (PBJ) determinations that serve as the legal triggers for the MVA's mandatory license revocation actions.

The bill's changes to license revocation and reinstatement for high-risk drivers directly impact this agency's customer base as the state's insurer of last resort and its role in processing hit-and-run claims.
The MSP is the primary agency responsible for enforcing the motor vehicle laws and investigating the fatal or life-threatening accidents that lead to the license revocations established by this bill.

The OAG acts as the primary legal advisor to the MVA and MDOT, and would represent the state in judicial challenges related to the interpretation and enforcement of the bill's revocation provisions.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive agencies implementing the bill and signed the legislation into law as part of its responsibility to enforce state laws and manage the state budget.

bill_summary: This bill modifies various provisions of Maryland's cannabis laws, primarily regarding on-site consumption establishments and dispensaries. It extends the authorization for converted medical cannabis dispensaries to deliver products to patients until July 1, 2026. It establishes a 'cannabis cafe' model for on-site consumption licensees, allowing them to operate as food service facilities and to repackage or process single-serving products and cannabinoid beverages. The bill also defines 'cannabinoid beverages' and ensures they are subject to the 9% cannabis sales and use tax rather than being exempt as food. Additionally, it limits on-site consumption license applications to social equity applicants under specific conditions, allows license transfers to employee stock ownership plans (ESOPs), and permits local governments to set hours of operation for consumption establishments.
responsible_party: Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA)
stakeholders: Cannabis dispensary and on-site consumption licensees, social equity applicants, medical cannabis patients and caregivers, and local political subdivisions.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Cannabis Administration may see a delay due to the repeal of the requirement to issue on-site consumption licenses during the second licensing round. However, the bill is not expected to materially affect State expenditures or local government finances. The bill clarifies that cannabinoid beverages are subject to the 9% cannabis sales and use tax.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary regulatory body for cannabis, the Maryland Cannabis Administration is the principal implementing agency for all provisions of the bill, including the oversight of on-site consumption licenses, dispensary supply requirements, and the regulation of cannabinoid beverages.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Cannabis Administration to consult with this office regarding disparity studies and the implementation of remedial measures for the second round of cannabis licensing to ensure participation by minority and women-owned businesses.

The bill excludes cannabinoid beverages from the standard food sales tax exemption, effectively subjecting them to the 9% cannabis sales and use tax, which the Comptroller is responsible for collecting and administering.

The Attorney General is named as a required consultant to evaluate the evidence of business discrimination in disparity studies and to ensure that the lottery system and remedial measures for cannabis licensing meet constitutional legal standards.

The bill allows on-site consumption establishments to operate as food service facilities, which are regulated by local health departments under the guidance of the Department of Health. It also references the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council, which is housed within the department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council, a specialized executive body, to establish the requirements for informational and educational materials that licensees must provide to consumers.

The Department of Commerce administers the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund (CBAF) to support small and minority-owned businesses; the bill's changes to the on-site consumption business model and social equity licensing have a significant economic impact on these stakeholders.

The bill references the Board of Public Works as the authority that designates the certification agency responsible for identifying Minority Business Enterprises, a designation critical to the issuance of cannabis licenses.

As the agency designated by the Board of Public Works for Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) certification, MDOT's data and certification processes are essential for the consultation and disparity study requirements outlined in the bill.

The bill is a departmental initiative from the Maryland Cannabis Administration, reflecting executive branch policy priorities on social equity and industry reform, which are overseen by the Governor's Office.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the qualification process for insurance producer licenses related to limited line credit insurance, credit life insurance, and credit health insurance. It removes the requirement for the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to approve the specific instructional programs provided by insurers. Instead, insurers must ensure these programs provide a comprehensive and accurate explanation of the insurance products and are required to maintain instructional records and participant lists for at least five years, making them available to the Commissioner upon request.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Applicants for limited line credit insurance producer licenses, insurance companies that sell or negotiate credit insurance products, and the Maryland Insurance Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect state expenditures or revenues, although it may lead to administrative efficiencies for the Maryland Insurance Administration. There is no fiscal impact on local governments, and the impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal or nonexistent.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) is the primary agency responsible for regulating the insurance industry and licensing insurance professionals. This departmental bill was introduced at the request of the MIA and directly alters the Insurance Commissioner's duties regarding the approval and oversight of training programs for limited line credit insurance producers.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the legal advisor to nearly all state agencies, including the Maryland Insurance Administration. It would provide legal counsel regarding the implementation of the new regulatory framework and the enforcement of the five-year record retention requirements for insurers.

The Office of Legislative Audits (OLA) conducts fiscal compliance and performance audits of executive agencies. OLA would be responsible for auditing the Maryland Insurance Administration to ensure it is properly enforcing the new record-keeping and request-based oversight procedures established by the bill.

As the chief executive, the Governor oversees the operations of all state departments, including the Maryland Insurance Administration. The Governor signed this departmental legislation into law and oversees the administration's broader regulatory policy.

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) serves as the state’s central fiscal authority and oversees the budget for the Maryland Insurance Administration. While the fiscal note indicates no material impact, DBM monitors the administrative efficiencies resulting from the shift away from mandatory course pre-approval.

bill_summary: This bill updates the Public Employee Relations Act (PERA) by allowing union representatives to meet with new employees via video technology regardless of public health conditions. It modifies the staffing requirements of the Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) to allow the appointment of up to three deputy directors, who must be licensed attorneys, instead of requiring three directors with specific subject-matter expertise. Additionally, it removes the 10-day minimum requirement for in-person voting in representation elections, allowing PERB to set the duration after consulting with the involved parties.
responsible_party: Public Employee Relations Board
stakeholders: Maryland public employees, public employers (including State agencies, public schools, and higher education institutions), and exclusive employee representatives (unions).
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates operational efficiencies for the State and potential future cost savings of more than $120,000 annually if the Public Employee Relations Board elects not to fill a third deputy director position. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by PERB. It directly alters the agency's internal staffing structure by changing the requirements and specialized roles of its deputy directors, including a new requirement that they be licensed attorneys. It also modifies the board's procedures for union meetings and election timelines.

The bill explicitly names the Office of Administrative Hearings as a venue for hearings on unfair labor practice complaints issued by the PERB. The fiscal note also indicates that OAH may need to train its administrative law judges on the substantive aspects of this bill.

As the state's central personnel and budget authority, DBM oversees the statewide personnel system and the funding for PERB positions. The bill's changes to the Public Employee Relations Act affect the framework for labor relations across the executive branch.

MDOT is identified in the fiscal note as a source of information for this bill. As a major state employer with significant bargaining units, MDOT's labor relations processes are governed by the Public Employee Relations Act being amended here.

The PERB oversees labor relations for the public school system. This bill removes the requirement for a specific deputy director at PERB dedicated solely to public school labor relations, potentially affecting how K-12 labor disputes are managed.

The USM's labor relations are governed by the PERB. The bill alters the structure of PERB's oversight, including the removal of a deputy director role specifically designated for higher education labor relations.

As a public higher education institution, Morgan State's collective bargaining is overseen by the PERB. Changes to PERB's administrative staffing and election procedures impact the university's labor relations framework.

Saint Mary's College is subject to the Public Employee Relations Act and PERB's jurisdiction. The modifications to PERB's operational procedures and staff qualifications affect the college's labor administration.

The OAG acts as the primary legal advisor for state agencies like PERB. The bill's requirement that PERB deputy directors be attorneys licensed in Maryland relates to the legal and prosecutorial functions coordinated through the state's chief legal office.

The Governor oversees executive branch operations and appoints the members of the Public Employee Relations Board. This departmental bill affects the structure and efficiency of an agency under the executive branch.

bill_summary: This bill increases various fees and penalties collected by the Maryland Department of the Environment to support its regulatory programs. Key changes include increasing air quality permit fee caps, raising the per-barrel oil transfer fee for five years, and expanding coal combustion by-product fees. Additionally, the bill establishes a regulatory framework for dam safety that requires private dam owners to register annually and pay fees into a new Private Dam Repair Fund, which will provide loans and financial assistance for the repair or removal of unsafe dams.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Private dam owners, oil transfer licensees, businesses requiring air quality permits, coal combustion by-product generators, and property owners using septic systems or individual wells.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase State special fund revenues by approximately $5.0 million in FY 2026, rising to $7.4 million by FY 2030. Special fund expenditures are projected to increase by $6.7 million in FY 2026 and by roughly $6.4 million to $6.5 million annually thereafter to implement the expanded programs. Local governments may experience minor cost increases to pay for higher fees associated with locally owned infrastructure such as landfills, wastewater plants, and dams.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for the bill, MDE is responsible for implementing the new fee structures for air quality permits, oil transfers, and coal combustion by-products. The department also administers the newly created Private Dam Repair Fund and oversees dam registration and safety inspections.

DBM is directly impacted by the bill's $6.7 million contingent appropriation in the FY 2026 budget. Additionally, the fiscal note identifies the need for new personnel (budget specialist and underwriter) to manage the Private Dam Repair Fund and loan program.
The bill is a departmental request from the executive branch. It requires the Secretary of MDE to report annually to the Governor on the status and financial health of the Private Dam Repair Fund.

MDOT (specifically the State Highway Administration) is identified as a dam owner that will be subject to new registration and permit fees. Additionally, the Maryland Port Administration is involved in the waterborne commerce of oil, which is subject to the increased transfer fees.

DNR is a major owner of state dams and water infrastructure, making it subject to the bill's new registration and permit fees. The agency also coordinates with MDE on water resource conservation and management.

The Comptroller is legally required to account for the multiple special funds modified or created by the bill, including the Clean Air Fund and the Private Dam Repair Fund, and to manage revenue from fee increases.

The State Treasurer is responsible for the custody and investment of the special funds mentioned in the bill. The bill explicitly directs that interest earnings from the Private Dam Repair Fund be credited back to the fund.
The OAG consults on annual enforcement reports and is authorized to bring legal actions to recover principal and interest from dam owners who default on loans provided by the Private Dam Repair Fund.

The bill affects the delegated authority of local health officers (who operate under MDH oversight) regarding on-site sewage disposal and well construction permits, authorizing MDE to collect fees if it assumes these permitting duties.
The bill's focus on dam safety, emergency action plans, and mitigating 'unsafe conditions' for aging infrastructure aligns with MDEM’s mission of hazard mitigation and statewide disaster resilience.
OLA will be responsible for auditing the financial management and compliance of the new and expanded special funds created by this legislation as part of its regular oversight of MDE.
The bill impacts how funds received from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which is managed by MEA, are deposited and utilized within the Maryland Clean Air Fund.
The bill includes specific exemptions for agricultural reservoirs and ponds from certain dam safety requirements, necessitating coordination between MDA and MDE on regulatory boundaries.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to issue research, development, and demonstration (RDD) permits for the incineration of chemical warfare materials at research facilities designated by the U.S. Department of Defense. While it exempts these facilities from certain general statutory requirements for controlled hazardous substance facilities when the incineration is for research purposes, it establishes new safety mandates including continuous air emissions monitoring, the development of emergency preparedness plans with public participation, and regular reporting to the state and the General Assembly.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: The U.S. Department of Defense (specifically the U.S. Army Chemical Biological Center at Aberdeen Proving Ground), residents and local governments in Maryland counties potentially impacted by chemical warfare material research, and state and local emergency response personnel.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not expected to be materially affected; the Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no direct impact on local government operations or finances, and the impact on small businesses is estimated to be minimal or nonexistent.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulatory agency for environmental protection, MDE is directly responsible for issuing the Research, Development, and Demonstration (RDD) permits, monitoring near-real-time air emissions, and enforcing safety standards for the incineration of chemical warfare materials.

The Department of Commerce requested this bill to facilitate research and development at federal facilities such as Aberdeen Proving Ground (APG), viewing these research technologies as vital to the state's economic and defense-related infrastructure.

The bill requires the development of emergency preparedness plans for 'maximum credible events' (toxic releases or explosions), involving the training and coordination of state and local emergency response personnel, which falls under MDEM's primary mission.

The incineration of highly toxic and carcinogenic chemical warfare materials directly impacts public health. The bill requires biennial assessments of the impact of these activities on public health and local ecosystems.
The Governor’s Office is responsible for signing the legislation and overseeing the executive departments (MDE and Commerce) tasked with implementing and managing the new permitting framework.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to the Maryland Department of the Environment and would be responsible for reviewing the legality of the RDD permits and representing the state in any environmental litigation arising from the permit process.

The Department of Labor's Maryland Occupational Safety and Health (MOSH) division ensures the safety of workers within the research facilities who may be exposed to hazardous chemical warfare materials during incineration processes.

The Adjutant General advises the Governor on state defense and security; since the bill regulates research facilities designated by the U.S. Department of Defense for warfare materials, it has implications for state-level defense security and coordination.

bill_summary: This bill requires each local board of elections in Maryland to submit a comprehensive election plan to the State Board of Elections for approval at least seven months before each statewide primary election. The election plan must consolidate polling place, ballot drop box, and early voting center plans, and include an analysis of how to maximize voter participation. The bill mandates public notice, local board meetings, and opportunities for public testimony before the adoption of an election plan, and requires specific consideration of the impact on historically disenfranchised communities.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections and local boards of elections
stakeholders: Maryland voters, local boards of elections, historically disenfranchised communities (including cultural, ethnic, and minority groups), and state and local elected officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances. It consolidates and modifies existing administrative requirements for election planning and approval that local and state boards of elections already perform. No significant impact on small businesses is anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill is directly focused on election administration, specifically requiring local boards of elections to submit consolidated election plans to the State Board of Elections (SBE) for approval and involving the State Administrator of Elections in the review process.

The OAG serves as the primary legal advisor to state agencies, including the State Board of Elections, and would be responsible for ensuring that the new election plan requirements and approval processes comply with constitutional and state law.

The bill mandates that election plans include an analysis of public transportation options available for voters to access polling places and early voting centers, which relates to the transit networks managed by MDOT business units like the MTA.

The bill's triggers for specific reporting requirements are based on 'statewide redistricting based on the census,' a process for which the Department of Planning provides the critical demographic and research data.

The bill requires local boards to include a determination regarding building compliance with the federal Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) in their polling place plans, aligning with the Department's mission to ensure equal access and independence for individuals with disabilities.

A core requirement of the bill is that the State Board must ensure election plans do not negatively affect access to voting for historically disenfranchised communities, which directly relates to the MCCR's mission to enforce anti-discrimination laws and ensure equal opportunity.

The Governor's Office oversees the operations of state departments and agencies like the State Board of Elections and is responsible for signing election law changes into effect to improve public equity and economic opportunity.

stakeholders: Employees of the office of a sheriff of a Maryland county or Baltimore City, county governments, and claimants in tort actions involving sheriff's office personnel.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in a minimal increase in State special fund expenditures for the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF) as it pays for tort claims involving sheriffs' employees. Local governments will see a minimal decrease in expenditures for litigation and payments related to these claims. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the principal executive agency, the Governor's Office oversees all state departments and signs legislation into law. This bill modifies the Maryland Tort Claims Act, which defines the state's liability and the legal protections afforded to personnel under the executive branch's purview.

The Maryland Tort Claims Act generally defines 'State personnel' as individuals paid by the Central Payroll Bureau, which is managed by the Comptroller. The bill specifically amends this section of the State Government Article to include employees of the office of a sheriff.

The State Treasurer's Office administers the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF), which is responsible for paying claims settled under the Maryland Tort Claims Act. The fiscal note indicates a direct increase in SITF special fund expenditures due to the expanded definition of state personnel.

The OAG represents state agencies and personnel in civil litigation. By expanding the definition of 'State personnel' under the Maryland Tort Claims Act, the OAG will be responsible for the legal defense of a broader pool of employees in tort actions.

DBM is the state's central fiscal authority and manages the statewide personnel system. It oversees the allocation of taxpayer resources and would be involved in the budgetary implications of increased premiums or assessments for the State Insurance Trust Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts the liability of personnel engaged in detention center and law enforcement functions, which are core areas of public safety. While sheriff offices are local, their state-level legal protections are relevant to the broader public safety and correctional policy landscape managed by DPSCS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP serves as the state's central hub for public safety policy. Since the bill directly affects the legal status and liability of law enforcement and administrative personnel within sheriff offices, it falls within the office's interest in coordinating statewide public safety initiatives.

Sheriff office employees, particularly court security officers and those involved in judicial protection, provide essential support to the Maryland Judiciary. Changes to their tort immunity and legal representation directly impact the personnel operating within court facilities.

The Board of Public Works protects the state's fiscal integrity and reviews significant state expenditures. Settlements or insurance premiums related to the expanded liability under the Maryland Tort Claims Act may eventually come under its oversight.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police has a vested interest in the legal protections and immunity standards provided to law enforcement-adjacent personnel in Maryland, including sheriff office employees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation passed by the General Assembly. As this bill was signed into law (Chapter 826), the office performed its primary constitutional function regarding this policy change.

The OAG serves as the primary legal advisor to the state and its agencies. It would be responsible for defending the state's new civil penalty structure in court if it were challenged by licensees in Baltimore City.

The Comptroller acts as the state's chief financial officer and 'tax collector' for alcoholic beverage revenues. While the fines in this bill are local to Baltimore City, the agency has a broader interest in the regulatory and licensing framework governing the state's alcohol industry.

The Department of Commerce is responsible for supporting small businesses and the hospitality industry. The establishment of mandatory minimum fines for hours-of-operation violations directly impacts the business environment for restaurants and bars in the state's largest city.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP advises on public safety policy. Regulating the hours of operation for establishments serving alcohol is a common tool used in municipal crime prevention strategies to manage late-night public safety and noise concerns.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Many alcoholic beverage license holders in Baltimore City are small or minority-owned businesses. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory reporting requirements of the Attorney General, who is mandated to pursue and report on economic damages recovery related to the Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse and Port of Baltimore closure.

The Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) is the agency responsible for the Francis Scott Key Bridge (a toll facility). The litigation and economic damage recovery reports being adjusted by the bill concern the loss and impact of this specific MDTA infrastructure.

The bill focuses on reports concerning the recovery of economic damages arising from the closure of the Helen Delich Bentley Port of Baltimore, which is managed and promoted by the Maryland Port Administration.

The Department of Transportation (MDOT) is the parent agency for both the Maryland Port Administration and the MDTA (which managed the Key Bridge). The status of litigation regarding the bridge collapse and port closure directly impacts MDOT's strategic and financial operations.

The Governor’s Office oversees executive branch agencies and led the initial response to the bridge collapse. The Attorney General is acting on behalf of the State to recover damages, a process of significant interest to the chief executive.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a regulatory and registration framework for virtual currency kiosks and their operators in Maryland. It requires operators to register each kiosk with the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, sets daily transaction limits of $2,000 for new users and $10,500 for experienced users, caps transaction fees at $5 or 15% of the transaction (whichever is greater), and mandates consumer protections such as on-screen risk disclosures, printed or digital receipts, and access to live customer support.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation in the Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Virtual currency kiosk owners and operators, Maryland consumers using virtual currency services, and the Maryland Department of Labor.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues are estimated to increase by $84,000 annually beginning in FY 2026, driven by registration fees ($2,000 per operator and $200 per kiosk). The Office of Financial Regulation is expected to implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, resulting in no additional state expenditures. There is no fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Commissioner of Financial Regulation as the primary official responsible for the registration, regulation, and enforcement of virtual currency kiosks. According to the agency summary, the Department of Labor encompasses the Office of Financial Regulation, which supervises the state’s financial services industry.

As the principal executive agency, the Governor's Office is responsible for signing or vetoing this legislation. The bill also impacts the state's annual budget through increased special fund revenues, which the Governor's Office oversees.

The OAG serves as the primary legal advisor to state agencies, including the Department of Labor. This bill involves significant consumer protection elements, such as fraud warnings and disclosure requirements, which align with the OAG's mission to prevent fraud and unfair business practices.

The bill authorizes the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to investigate, enforce, and assess civil penalties. Actions taken by state regulatory agencies are typically subject to challenge in the OAH, where Administrative Law Judges resolve contested cases.
The bill is expected to increase special fund revenues by an estimated $84,000 annually. DBM is responsible for estimating state revenues and overseeing the fiscal operations of the executive branch.

The fiscal note identifies a meaningful impact on small businesses that operate virtual currency kiosks. As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce may be involved in supporting these small businesses as they navigate new registration fees and operational requirements.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the requirements for the party affiliation of chief election judges at polling places. It requires that each polling place have an equal number of chief judges and other election judges from the majority and principal minority parties to the extent practicable. If a local election director is unable to designate one chief judge from each of those parties at least 45 days before early voting starts, they must designate one judge from a major party and one who is not registered with either party.

The Department of Human Services is explicitly named as a state agency through which outreach mechanisms for veterans, service members, and their families must be disseminated.

The bill addresses youth suicide and behavioral health, which are public health priorities for the Department. The agency leads a 'whole-of-government' approach to child well-being. This bill directly aligns with its mission to coordinate state agency efforts to address student behavioral health, trauma, and expanded access to mental health services for youth.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency regulates the state's commercial gaming and sports wagering industries. Since the bill specifically mandates instruction on the relationship between gambling and youth suicide, the agency's responsible gambling programs and industry oversight are contextually linked to the bill's objectives.

The Governor's Office oversees the operations of all state departments involved in the program and signed the bill into law. Improving child well-being and public safety are key initiatives of the office mentioned in the preamble.

Operating within the Department of Education, this independent unit is dedicated to fostering safe and inclusive learning environments and provides training and technical assistance related to student well-being and behavioral threat assessments.

As an independent state agency that functions as a public school for deaf and hard-of-hearing residents, the agency must ensure its students have access to the mandated suicide prevention and awareness programming required by the bill.

The Department serves as the state's central fiscal authority and manages the statewide personnel system. It would oversee any fiscal changes or administrative regulations required for MSDE and MDH to implement the expanded program.

The fiscal note indicates the program was historically supported by federal grants. This office coordinates state activities to identify and manage the federal funds that could support youth suicide prevention initiatives.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency advises on public safety policy and administers grants that support local governments and nonprofits in reducing youth violence and addressing substance abuse, which the bill identifies as factors related to suicide risk.
The agency provides child welfare services and protective oversight for vulnerable youth, a population that often requires behavioral health referrals and trauma-informed care mentioned in the bill.

The agency manages youth involved in the justice system, many of whom experience the trauma, addiction, and behavioral health issues that the bill aims to address through improved identification and referral protocols.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards

The office tracks progress on the Governor's key priorities, including improving health outcomes and community safety, and may monitor the effectiveness of the expanded suicide prevention program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office advocates for inclusive access to state services; it would be concerned with ensuring that classroom instruction regarding gambling and suicide is accessible to students who are deaf or hard of hearing.
The Lieutenant Governor leads statewide initiatives focused on public safety and mental health, which are directly relevant to the policy objectives of this bill.
The team focuses on data-driven solutions for economic mobility and childhood well-being; the bill's focus on identifying students experiencing out-of-school trauma aligns with their mission.

bill_summary: This bill requires that during the migratory Canada goose hunting season, the daily bag limit for all Canada geese in most parts of Maryland must match the limits set annually by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service for the Atlantic population. The bill excludes Allegany, Frederick, Garrett, and Washington counties, and the western portion of Carroll County from this requirement.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Hunters, farmers, and small businesses affected by resident goose populations in Montgomery, Charles, and Prince George's counties.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances. It may have a meaningful impact on small businesses, particularly farms, by potentially reducing the harvest of resident geese in specific zones, which could lead to increased agricultural damage.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary agency responsible for managing Maryland's living resources and regulating hunting. The bill directly mandates that DNR set hunting bag limits for Canada geese in specific zones to conform with federal standards during the migratory season, directly affecting their regulatory and enforcement duties.

The bill restricts hunting bag limits for resident Canada geese in certain areas, which may lead to higher populations of these birds. bill_summary: Senate Bill 338 authorizes the Maryland State Highway Administration (SHA) to install and operate speed monitoring systems on Interstate 695 and Interstate 83 within Baltimore County. The bill establishes a $40 maximum civil penalty for violations and requires that the collected revenue be used to recover the costs of implementing the systems and to fund roadway and safety improvements on those specific highways. It includes requirements for public notice, signage, and annual reporting, and mandates that warning notices be issued during the first 30 days of operation.
responsible_party: Maryland State Highway Administration
stakeholders: Motorists driving on Interstate 695 and Interstate 83 in Baltimore County, the Maryland State Highway Administration, the Maryland Department of State Police, and the residents of Baltimore County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues for the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) are expected to increase from the collection of $40 civil penalties, with corresponding increases in TTF expenditures to cover administrative costs (estimated at up to $600,000 annually) and roadway safety improvements. A one-time general fund expenditure of $12,208 is required in FY 2026 for the Judiciary to perform system reprogramming. Local government finances are not directly affected, although Baltimore County may benefit from the funded highway improvements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes the State Highway Administration (SHA), a business unit of MDOT, to place and use speed monitoring systems on Interstates 695 and 83 in Baltimore County. SHA is responsible for implementing the program, identifying high-risk locations, and using the resulting revenue for roadway safety improvements.

The bill designates Maryland State Police (MSP) officers as speed monitoring system operators, involves the agency in identifying high-risk locations for camera placement, and requires MSP to jointly adopt program regulations with SHA.

The bill authorizes 'the Administration' (MVA) to refuse or suspend motor vehicle registrations if a person fails to pay civil penalties or contest violations recorded by the speed monitoring systems.
The District Court, supported by the AOC, is responsible for processing citations, prescribing uniform forms, collecting civil penalties, and adjudicating cases where motorists elect to stand trial.
The bill requires that fines collected by the District Court for these specific violations be remitted to the Comptroller for distribution to the State Highway Administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission, which is part of DPSCS, is tasked with developing training for the program and compiling an annual report on the operation and revenue of speed monitoring systems.

The bill impacts the state budget by creating a new revenue stream for the Transportation Trust Fund and mandates that these funds supplement, rather than supplant, existing appropriations, requiring fiscal oversight from DBM.

The Governor's Office oversees the implementing executive agencies and is the recipient of multiple reports mandated by the bill, including an annual report from the Police Training and Standards Commission and a 2029 evaluation report from SHA.

The bill specifies that the procurement of speed monitoring systems must follow state procurement law; the BPW may be required to review and approve significant contracts related to the system's deployment and maintenance.

The bill explicitly prohibits insurance companies from considering speed monitoring system violations in the provision of coverage; the MIA regulates insurers to ensure compliance with such consumer protection statutes.
The OAG serves as the legal advisor to SHA, MSP, and the District Court, and may be involved in drafting the required regulations or defending legal challenges to the new enforcement program.

OLA will likely review the fiscal compliance and management of the newly authorized speed camera revenues during its periodic audits of the Maryland Department of Transportation and the District Court.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes organizations affiliated with a professional major league baseball team that plays home games in Baltimore City to conduct raffles. It requires these organizations to obtain a permit from a designated Baltimore City agency, use age-verification measures for buyers (who must be at least 18 years old), and utilize geofencing to ensure electronic ticket sales occur within a specific geographical area of Baltimore City.
responsible_party: An agency designated by the Baltimore City government (such as the Baltimore City Police Department)
stakeholders: Organizations affiliated with professional major league baseball teams in Baltimore City and raffle participants aged 18 and older.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material impact on state or local finances. State finances are not affected, though a negligible decrease in lottery revenues may occur due to substitution effects. Baltimore City can implement the permit process using existing resources, and the fiscal impact on the city is not material.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill focuses on raffles conducted at professional major league baseball games in Baltimore City and defines a geofenced area for electronic raffles that aligns with the boundaries of the Camden Yards Sports Complex, which the Stadium Authority is responsible for managing and maintaining.

The Governor's Office is responsible for signing or vetoing the legislation and overseeing the coordination of state agencies mentioned as information sources for the bill's impact analysis.

The OAG acts as the primary legal advisor to the General Assembly and would be responsible for reviewing the legality of the new geofencing and electronic raffle provisions within the state's Criminal Law Article.

The bill impacts the operations and fundraising capabilities of an organization affiliated with a professional sports team, which falls under the agency's mission to stimulate economic growth and support major private investment sectors.

As an agency that promotes Maryland and Baltimore as premier travel destinations, the bill relates to enhancing the visitor experience and activities at a major professional sports venue, which is a significant tourist attraction.

The agency is listed as an information source for the fiscal note and maintains statewide jurisdiction over the investigation of major crimes and criminal law violations, including the new misdemeanor provisions established by the bill.
The Comptroller's Office is identified as an information source for the fiscal note regarding the bill's impact on state revenues and lottery-related fiscal forecasting.
The bill establishes new criminal violations and misdemeanor penalties, which would be processed through the state judicial system and its public records infrastructure managed by the AOC.

bill_summary: This bill expands the legal definition of 'visual representation' within the context of revenge porn to include computer-generated images (such as deepfakes) that are indistinguishable from an actual person. It creates a civil cause of action for defamation per se or invasion of privacy for victims whose visual representations are distributed without consent, allowing them to seek attorney's fees. The bill also protects these images in court records from public inspection.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and State's Attorneys
stakeholders: Victims of revenge porn, including those depicted in computer-generated images; legal professionals; law enforcement; and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill may result in a minimal increase in State and local revenues and expenditures due to the expanded application of existing criminal penalties. The Judiciary anticipates that any increase in civil case filings can be handled with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new civil cause of action for defamation and invasion of privacy related to revenge porn. It also significantly modifies court record accessibility by restricting the public inspection of visual representations and computer-generated images in both criminal and civil cases, directly impacting the Judiciary's record management and information systems like Case Search.

The bill explicitly names the Attorney General or their designee as one of the parties authorized to inspect sensitive visual representations within court records. Additionally, the OAG provides legal counsel and manages appeals related to the criminal and civil statutes modified by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the scope of the criminal offense of 'revenge porn' to include computer-generated visual representations. As the primary provider of legal representation for indigent residents facing criminal charges where incarceration is possible (the misdemeanor carries up to 2 years), the OPD will be directly responsible for defending individuals charged under this updated statute.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency responsible for investigating major and cyber-related crimes, the MSP is responsible for enforcing the criminal provisions of the bill. Law enforcement officers are also explicitly listed as parties allowed to inspect visual evidence in restricted court records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP serves as the state’s hub for public safety policy and advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies. This bill updates public safety laws regarding non-consensual imagery and computer-generated 'deepfakes,' which falls under their policy purview.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies a criminal offense punishable by up to two years of imprisonment. While most misdemeanor sentences are served in local jails, the DPSCS may be impacted by changes in community supervision (parole and probation) for offenders convicted under the expanded statute.

The Governor signed this legislation into law. The office is responsible for overseeing state initiatives aimed at improving public safety and enforcing state laws, which includes the new protections against revenge porn.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, MDH is responsible for compiling and submitting quarterly reports on disaggregated nursing home inspection data. Its internal unit, the Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), is specifically tasked with providing biannual reports to local area agencies on aging regarding specific survey dates and facility names.

The new disaggregated inspection data generated by this bill directly supports the MHCC's mission to provide consumers with health quality data.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts the work of the Oversight Committee on Quality of Care in Nursing Homes and Assisted Living Facilities, which evaluates progress in improving facility care. OHCQ is already required to report to this committee, and the additional reporting mandates in this bill further inform the committee's policy recommendations.

The OLA conducts fiscal and compliance audits of executive agencies. Because this bill creates new statutory reporting mandates for the Maryland Department of Health, OLA will be responsible for verifying compliance with these reporting requirements during its periodic audits of the department.

The Governor's Office oversees the operations of the Maryland Department of Health and signed this legislation into law. The office maintains high-level executive interest in the efficiency of the Office of Health Care Quality and the safety of residents in state-licensed nursing homes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to annually review a report published by the Independent Investigations Division (IID). agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC) is the primary agency tasked with the review and recommendations required by the bill. In Maryland, the MPTSC is an independent unit that is administratively housed within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is subject to the training and certification standards set by the MPTSC. Recommendations made by the Commission following a review of investigations into police-involved fatalities directly impact the MSP’s operational and training standards.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency serves as the state’s central hub for public safety policy and advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies. The policy recommendations generated by the MPTSC regarding police-involved incidents are highly relevant to this office's mission to improve public safety and justice outcomes.

bill_summary: This bill expands eligibility for the State of Maryland's public safety death benefits to include 9-1-1 specialists. It also establishes a legal presumption that a public safety officer's death by suicide is a result of injuries sustained in the performance of their duties, provided the individual was diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), acute stress disorder, or a trauma-related disorder resulting from their job duties.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: 9-1-1 specialists, law enforcement officers, correctional officers, firefighters, rescue squad members, public safety aviation employees, and their surviving families or estates.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have no immediate material effect on State expenditures because the expanded eligibility is likely to apply in only a limited number of cases. Any increases in death benefit payments can likely be covered by funds typically budgeted for this purpose, such as the $850,000 included in the fiscal 2026 budget. There is no fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary agency responsible for administering the public safety death benefit. The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services makes determinations on eligibility, notifies potential recipients, and processes applications for the $125,000 benefit.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Secretary of State issue a State flag to the family of any qualifying public safety officer or military member killed in the performance of duty.
The DVMF is specifically tasked with presenting the State flag to the families of deceased military members who qualify for the death benefits established or expanded under this bill.

The Governor is responsible for including funding for the death and funeral benefits in the annual State budget, and the bill clarifies the circumstances under which these executive funds must be allocated.

The bill adds 9-1-1 specialists to the list of eligible recipients for state death benefits. MDEM oversees the state's 9-1-1 system and emergency communication infrastructure, directly involving the professional group newly covered by the bill.
The bill includes hazardous material response team employees of the Department of the Environment as eligible individuals for the public safety death benefits and funeral expenses.

DBM oversees the state budget and personnel fiscal authority. Since the benefits are paid from funds included by the Governor in the budget, DBM is involved in the fiscal management and allocation of these increased expenditures.

MSP personnel, including law enforcement officers and public safety aviation employees, are primary beneficiaries of the death benefit program. The bill's new presumption regarding suicide and PTSD diagnoses directly impacts MSP members and their families.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides benefits to emergency medical services providers, who are regulated and coordinated by MIEMSS. The definitions of these providers in the bill refer to the Education Article which governs MIEMSS's oversight.

bill_summary: The bill allows for the construction of overhead transmission lines through the Big Savage Mountain, Bear Pen, and Dan’s Mountain Wildlands by exempting specific corridors from wildland protection status. To proceed, an applicant must obtain a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN), replace any lost wildland acreage with new land that is twice the size of the area lost, and develop a conservation management plan to support wildlife habitats. The bill also establishes a 120-day stakeholder participation process and requires a recommendation from the Secretary of Natural Resources before construction can be approved.
responsible_party: Maryland Public Service Commission and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Electric utility customers in Maryland and the surrounding region, NextEra Energy Transmission MidAtlantic, Inc., PJM Interconnection, LLC, environmental and conservation organizations, and residents of Allegany and Garrett counties.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances. While there is a potential risk to federal Pittman-Robertson Wildlife Restoration Act funding if wildland acreage is lost and not replaced, the bill mandates that the transmission line applicant provide replacement acreage at twice the size of the lost land. The Department of Natural Resources and the Public Service Commission expect to handle the administrative requirements of the bill using existing resources. Local governments in Allegany and Garrett counties will be involved in the review and permitting process but will not see a significant fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Public Utilities Article to require the Commission to mandate wildland impact mitigation guarantees for certain overhead transmission lines and to consider aviation safety, environmental impacts, and alternate routes during the CPCN process.

DNR manages the State wildlands preservation system affected by this bill. The bill requires the Secretary of Natural Resources to recommend a CPCN and tasks the department with a 90-day deliberation period and the oversight of wildland mitigation acreage replacement.

As the independent state agency representing residential utility consumers before the Public Service Commission, the OPC is a primary stakeholder in CPCN proceedings regarding electric transmission infrastructure and reliability.

The bill's preamble and the Public Utilities Article amendments specifically name the Maryland Aviation Administration as a determining body for assessing the effect of overhead transmission lines on aviation safety.

The bill requires a recommendation from the Secretary of Natural Resources (a cabinet official) and involves the Governor's authority to oversee state agencies and sign legislation affecting state land designations.

The OAG serves as the primary legal advisor to the Public Service Commission and the Department of Natural Resources, both of which face new regulatory requirements and complex legal questions regarding wildland exemptions and mitigation guarantees.

As the parent agency of the Maryland Aviation Administration and the State Highway Administration, MDOT is impacted by assessments of aviation safety and potential infrastructure impacts where transmission lines intersect state-managed rights-of-way.

The Public Service Commission must consider air quality and water pollution impacts of transmission lines, areas where MDE provides regulatory oversight and technical evaluation during the CPCN process.

MEA is involved in state energy policy and managing the Strategic Energy Investment Fund; it has a vested interest in the stability and reliability of the electric grid mentioned in the bill's preamble.
The wildland areas in Garrett and Allegany counties are significant natural assets for heritage and nature-based tourism in Western Maryland, which this office promotes.
The council advocates for the 18 rural counties of Maryland, including Garrett and Allegany, where the impacted wildlands and proposed transmission infrastructure are located.

This multi-agency initiative coordinates smart growth and environmental stewardship efforts between DNR, MDE, and other agencies, all of which are involved in balancing infrastructure needs with wildland preservation.

bill_summary: This bill updates the fee structure for generators of coal combustion by-products (CCB), such as coal ash, by setting a minimum base fee of $2.30 per ton and incorporating the volume of stored by-products into fee calculations. It establishes the Statewide Coal Combustion By-Products Coordinating Committee to facilitate information sharing and monitor remedial actions at storage sites. Additionally, the bill requires the Maryland Department of the Environment to adopt regulations for federal legacy coal combustion residual rules and mandates that any excess fee revenue be used for beneficial reuse initiatives and mitigating health and environmental impacts at priority sites.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment and the Power Plant Research Program in the Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Generators of coal combustion by-products, coal-fired power plant operators, residents near coal combustion by-product disposal and storage sites, and environmental health advocates.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues are projected to increase by approximately $1,031,300 in FY 2027 and $1,102,600 by FY 2030 due to the expanded fee structure. Special fund expenditures increase by $200,000 in FY 2026 (contingent upon the enactment of this bill) to cover regulatory costs, with slight annual increases for administrative ongoing costs in subsequent years. The bill is expected to have a minimal or no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency. It is responsible for establishing and collecting fees from coal combustion by-product (CCB) generators, using excess revenues for beneficial reuse and mitigation projects, adopting regulations to implement federal rules on legacy coal ash, and chairing the new Statewide CCB Coordinating Committee.

The bill explicitly tasks the Power Plant Research Program (PPRP), located within DNR, with providing a representative to the Coordinating Committee and jointly staffing the committee with MDE. The fiscal note also highlights DNR's role in tracking and evaluating CCB sites.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Statewide Coal Combustion By-Products Coordinating Committee as a new executive body to share monitoring information and discuss remedial actions across state agencies and commissions.

The Coordinating Committee is required to include a member with technical expertise in public health, and MDE is mandated to use fee revenues to mitigate human health impacts resulting from the release of coal combustion by-products.

DBM oversees the state budget and personnel. The fiscal note indicates a specific special fund expenditure increase of $200,000 for FY 2026 contingent on this legislation, and DBM would manage the associated budgetary adjustments.

MES is listed as a primary information source in the fiscal note. As a fee-for-service agency that manages large-scale environmental and waste projects, they are likely to be involved in the implementation of the remedial and mitigation actions funded by the CCB Management Fund.

The OAG would provide legal counsel to MDE for the development and adoption of the mandatory regulations regarding legacy coal combustion residuals and the operation of the new Coordinating Committee.

The PSC regulates the power plants that generate coal combustion by-products. Changes to fees and regulatory standards for CCBs impact the operations and costs of the utilities under the PSC's jurisdiction.

The bill requires the Governor to approve the legislation and the Secretary of the Environment (a cabinet-level official appointed by the Governor) to designate the chair of the new Coordinating Committee and appoint technical experts.

This multi-agency initiative coordinates the work of MDE and DNR on environmental stewardship and sustainable growth. The bill's focus on coal ash management and beneficial reuse aligns directly with its mission.

As the state's fiscal watchdog and collector of revenues, the Comptroller monitors the management of the Coal Combustion By-Products Management Fund and sits on the Board of Public Works which may review related contracts.

OLA conducts fiscal and compliance audits of state agencies. The establishment of new fee structures and a specific special fund expenditure plan for CCB revenues would likely be a focus of future OLA audits of MDE.

bill_summary: The Registered Apprenticeship Investments for a Stronger Economy (RAISE) Act expands Maryland's workforce development efforts by establishing the Maryland Office of Registered Apprenticeship Development (MORAD) to market and scale apprenticeship programs across various industries. It creates the Registered Apprenticeship Qualified Intermediary Program to connect employers with training partners and the Maryland Pay Per Apprentice Program to provide financial incentives to employers and sponsors for hiring new apprentices. The bill also mandates specific journeyworker-to-apprentice ratios and establishes an advisory board to guide the State's apprenticeship expansion strategy.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Maryland employers, registered apprentices, apprenticeship sponsors, labor organizations, and workforce development partners.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1.5 million in FY 2026 to fund 14 new administrative positions (Apprenticeship Navigators) for MORAD. Between FY 2027 and FY 2030, the Governor may provide at least $5 million annually to the Maryland Pay Per Apprentice Program Fund, leading to a significant increase in special fund revenues and expenditures for apprentice grants. Local governments may see a minimal fiscal impact if they apply for and receive grants. Small businesses are expected to experience a meaningful economic impact through direct financial incentives and improved access to a skilled workforce.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the Department of Labor is responsible for establishing and managing the Maryland Office of Registered Apprenticeship Development, the Qualified Intermediary Program, and the Pay Per Apprentice Program. The Department also administers the newly created special fund and oversees the Apprenticeship and Training Council.

The bill explicitly requires the Director of the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program to consult with the Governor's Workforce Development Board in the development of the Registered Apprenticeship Qualified Intermediary Program.

The bill has a significant fiscal impact, requiring the Governor to include appropriations for the administrative costs of the new office and authorized appropriations for the incentive fund. DBM will oversee the allocation of funds and the 14 new positions identified in the fiscal note.

This is an Administration bill that aligns with the Governor's priorities on economic mobility. The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the new advisory board and mandating budget appropriations for the apprenticeship programs.

The bill requires the Department of Commerce to be consulted during the development of the Registered Apprenticeship Qualified Intermediary Program to ensure alignment with the state's economic needs.
The bill mandates that the State Treasurer hold the Maryland Apprenticeship Incentive Pay Per Apprentice Program Fund separately and invest its funds in the same manner as other State money.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the newly established Maryland Apprenticeship Incentive Pay Per Apprentice Program Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Registered Apprenticeship Development Advisory Board within the Department of Labor to advise on strategies for expanding apprenticeship opportunities.

The bill repeals the Youth Apprenticeship Advisory Committee, which included the State Superintendent, and alters the landscape of apprenticeship programs that MSDE coordinates with for youth and high school students.

The bill requires new reporting on worker outcomes, including post-apprenticeship wage rates and job placement data, which directly pertains to the MLDS mission of linking education and workforce data.

The OAG serves as the legal advisor to the Department of Labor and would assist in the drafting of regulations and the legal structuring of the new grants and procurement processes authorized by the bill.
The bill repeals the Youth Apprenticeship Advisory Committee, on which the Secretary of Juvenile Services served as a statutory member.

The Office of Appointments would be responsible for the recruitment and vetting of the employer representatives and the chair for the newly created Registered Apprenticeship Development Advisory Board.
